title: Redfern's Outpost
summary: A top-down pixel adventure about a mountain man holding down a lonely outpost in the pines.
description:
You are Redfern, keeping a palisaded outpost in the pines: two log cabins, a well, a pond to the north, and a trail that disappears south into the forest.

Redfern carries the Fernbrand, one tool that can't be dropped and changes shape instead. As a timber axe it fells trees; as a lash it drags loot to your hand; fed with tusks it becomes a pick you brace against a charging boar. Each shape climbs its own ranks, from Novice to Legend.

The seasons turn, the year goes by, and Redfern ages with it. It started life as a Game Boy Advance prototype and is now being built in Godot with full-colour pixel art.
features: The Fernbrand: one blade, many shapes, each with its own ranks
Hunting: deer that bolt, boars that charge
Fishing, camping and a town to trade with
Four seasons, a calendar, and a hero who grows older
Hand-made 32 px pixel art

title: Chao World: Seasons
summary: Chao World as a game of its own on the PS Vita: the Chao garden from Sonic Adventure 2: Battle, grown into a full year of seasons.
description:
Chao World: Seasons is a Chao World game made for the PS Vita. It started with the Chao World inside Sonic Adventure 2: Battle on the GameCube: the gardens, the Chao and everything you do with them, taken out of the main game with no stages and no story. From there it was built out into a bigger Chao World of its own.

The year turns: spring, summer, autumn and winter, with day and night, rainy days and festivals in the lobby. Every Chao has a personality, a family, dreams and favourite things, and grows up at the pace you care for it. There's a Chao Games tournament every season, a photo mode, a journal, fishing, garden decorating and new places to visit.

Some of the extras rebuild favourite features from the Chao World Extended and Enhanced Chao World mods for PC.
features: Just the Chao World: no stages, no story, every character playable
Four seasons, day and night, rainy days and lobby festivals
Livelier Chao: personalities, families, dreams and rare Chao
The Chao Games each season: race, karate and a swim, alone or as a team of three
Photo mode, a Chao Journal, fishing and garden decorating
New places, like the Station Square Garden and the Chao Refuge
Features from the Chao World Extended and Enhanced Chao World mods, rebuilt
note: A fan project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by SEGA. Sonic Adventure 2, Sonic and Chao are trademarks of SEGA. Seasons runs on data from your own copy of the game, and no game files are distributed here.

title: Tinbox
summary: A Game Boy Advance emulator for iPhone and iPad, built on the mGBA core.
description:
Tinbox is a native iOS Game Boy Advance player, with a SwiftUI interface, Metal rendering and the accurate mGBA core underneath.

It keeps your library tidy, plays in portrait or landscape, and has save states, themes and skins.
features: mGBA core, rendered with Metal
Portrait and landscape play
Save states and a quick menu
Themes and skins
Bluetooth controller support
screenshotNote: The game shown is Tobu Tobu Girl Deluxe, a free homebrew game.
note: Tinbox doesn't come with any games. Play games you own or free homebrew.

title: Packmule
summary: A free file mule for iOS. Haul files between your phone and anything that speaks SMB, FTP or SFTP.
description:
Packmule moves files between your phone and Windows shares, NAS boxes, Linux machines and other phones. It can also host: start its built-in FTP server and other devices connect to the phone.

Free means free. SMB, FTP, uploads, downloads: all of it. There's no Pro tier, no subscription and no unlock. A file app shouldn't ransom your own files back to you.
features: SMB2/3 shares, FTP and SFTP
Stream movies and music straight from a share, no download first
Jellyfin: sign in, browse and stream
Built-in FTP server to host files from the phone
No ads, no subscription, no Pro tier

title: DevBazaar
summary: A marketplace where indie devs hand off games they can't finish, trade assets and find collaborators, with a signed agreement and escrow on every deal.
description:
DevBazaar is a marketplace built for indie game developers. Sometimes a project stalls because you ran out of time, money or spark, not because the idea was bad. DevBazaar lets you hand it to someone who'll finish it.

The Unfinished aisle has prototypes, vertical slices and nearly-finished games looking for a new owner, with their progress, engine and exactly what's included. The Assets aisle has tilesets, music, sound effects and code to buy outright, license or trade for something of your own. And the notice board is where projects find artists, composers and programmers, for paid, rev-share or hobby work.

Haggling's welcome: offer cash, a trade or both. When a deal is struck, both sides sign a written rights agreement and the money sits in escrow until the work is delivered. Set up like a night market, with hand-painted signs, price tags and a resident raven, DevBazaar is a friendlier place to pass a project on.
features: Sell, license or trade unfinished games and assets
Haggle with cash, trades, or both
A rights agreement both sides sign on every deal
Escrow: sellers get paid when buyers confirm delivery
Collaborator notice board for paid, rev-share or hobby projects
AI-use disclosure on every listing, with a filter
5% fee, taken from the seller's side only when a sale completes
screenshotNote: The screenshots show sample listings and people from the demo data, not real users.
note: DevBazaar isn't open yet. Payments run in test mode until launch.
